title: Handlebar Remote
tagline: A slim thumb controller between the grip and the switch cube, for the dash and your phone
summary: One slim collar on the left handlebar, between the grip and the bike's switch cube: a 5-way joystick at the back under your thumb, on its own raised platform angled toward your hand, and 4 buttons going up over the top of the bar, on a face curved round the bar and tilted toward the grip, so nothing stands higher than the switch cube and it hides none of the bike's own instruments. The electronics sit in a slim capsule underneath (the ESP32 lying lengthwise), closed by a rubber plug, with a button and 2 status LEDs at its back, facing you. It works the Handlebar Dash over its own wiring (one of the dash's expansion slots) and a phone or anything else over Bluetooth, as a keyboard with media keys. One smooth, rounded body: the switches in 2 printed carriers inside the face, a printed TPU keypad that seals it, the halves hinged at the back and closed by one hidden screw. General purpose: the bar size, the gap and the angles are settings.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). The switches and boards have no published drawings: measure yours first, and the gap you can make between the grip and the switch cube. The firmware comes next.
see_sub: One smooth collar, 19 mm wide, in a 20 mm gap between the grip and the switch cube (slide the cube inboard to make it): the controls on a face curved round the back and the top of the bar, its highest point 27.3 mm above the bar's centre (the cube's top is at 30); the joystick on its own platform; the ESP32-C3 lying lengthwise in a 13 mm wide capsule underneath, its button and LEDs at the back.

gallery.caption: From the rider's seat: the collar between the grip and the switch cube (grey: a stand-in; measure yours), no higher than the cube: the joystick on its platform at the back under the thumb, the buttons over the top, the slim capsule underneath
From the rider's side: the joystick on its own raised platform, angled toward the hand; buttons 1 and 2 (round) and 3 and 4 (pills) going up over the bar, each in its own cup
Along the bar: the face curves round the back and the top of the bar, the joystick's platform at the back; the hinge under it, the slim capsule turned a little forward
From above: 19 mm wide along the bar, in the gap between the grip and the switch cube
The capsule under the bar, its plugs and back pad pulled off: the ESP32-C3 lies lengthwise inside with the CAN transceiver on its back; the dash's cable goes through the bottom plug
The capsule's back, facing you: the button (dash / phone; held: Bluetooth pairing) and the 2 status LEDs (power, Bluetooth)

Taken apart: the collar's top half (with the face and the joystick's platform) lifted, the keypad, the 2 switch carriers with their switches, the joystick's cap, the bottom half swung open on its hinge, the capsule's plug

docs.label: README: what it does, how it's built, the wiring and the dash-bus messages

collar_top.name: Collar top (with the face)
collar_top.what: The smooth body's upper half: the ring's top and the face curved round the back and the top of the bar, with the joystick's raised platform (its hole), a cup round each button's hole and the ridge, hollow inside and open toward the bar for the keypad and the switch carriers; 2 hinge knuckles at the back, the front screw's insert
collar_top.material: ASA (PETG for a first try), 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

collar_bottom.name: Collar bottom (with the capsule)
collar_bottom.what: The smooth body's lower half: the ring's bottom and the slim electronics capsule (the ESP32-C3 lying lengthwise, the CAN transceiver on its back, the button board at the back), open at the bottom for its plug; the USB-C hole in its front, the button's and LEDs' holes in its back; the middle hinge knuckle; the front screw comes up through it into the top half
collar_bottom.material: ASA / PETG, 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

carrier_joy.name: Switch carrier: joystick + button 1
carrier_joy.what: Holds the 5-way switch on a pedestal up in its platform (its legs through it, a well underneath for their wires) and button 1's tactile switch in a flat pocket; goes up into the top half from the bar's side, first, pressing the keypad against the face
carrier_joy.material: ASA / PETG. On its flat switch-cube side

carrier_btn.name: Switch carrier: buttons 2-4
carrier_btn.what: Holds the other tactile switches (buttons 2 to 4; button 2 only with 2 buttons) the same way; goes in after the joystick's carrier
carrier_btn.material: ASA / PETG. On its flat switch-cube side

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: A TPU liner inside the face, in one piece: the sheet under the face (its hollow domes are the buttons, round and pills), a turret rising into the joystick's platform round its switch (it hugs the cap's sleeve), and a skirt round its edge; the carriers squeeze the skirt and the turret's foot against the face: the seal
keypad.material: TPU 85A-95A. As an arch, its sheet on top (supports under it)

joy_cap.name: Joystick cap
joy_cap.what: A low 13 mm mushroom cap that pushes onto the 5-way switch's stem
joy_cap.material: ASA / PETG, or TPU for grip. Flat top down

bay_plug.name: Capsule plug
bay_plug.what: Closes the capsule from below, no screws: a rounded flange and a plug 0.1 mm tight in the mouth (the seal) with a bead that snaps into its groove; the dash's cable goes through it (it grips the cable). Pull it by its ridge to reach the ESP32's USB-C

back_pad.name: Back pad
back_pad.what: Inside the capsule's back wall: a dome through the button's hole (press it), holes that hug the 2 LEDs; the button's switch squeezes it against the wall (the seal)

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Closes the ESP32's USB-C in the capsule's front wall; a ridge to pull it by

remote_assembled.name: Assembled
remote_assembled.what: The collar on the bar, with stand-ins for the grip, the switch cube and the boards

params.name: buttons
params.label: Buttons
choices: 4 (up over the top of the bar)
params.help: In one column above the joystick: the collar is too narrow for two.

params.name: bar_d
params.label: Handlebar diameter
params.help: 22.2 (7/8") or 25.4 (1"). A bigger bar puts the face higher: the model refuses anything above the switch cube's top.

params.name: gap_w
params.label: Gap between the grip and the switch cube
params.help: The collar is 1 mm narrower. Slide the switch cube inboard to make room. At least 20 mm (the joystick's tilted switch needs the width).

params.name: joy_a
params.label: Where the joystick sits, round the bar
params.help: From straight forward: 180 = straight back toward you, level with the bar's centre; 190 = a little below it. The buttons follow it up over the top.

params.name: pod_tilt
params.label: Controls tilted toward the grip
params.help: So your thumb reaches them straight from the grip.

params.name: joy_rise
params.label: The joystick's platform: how proud of the face
params.help: Its own flat top, on a separate plane from the buttons.

params.name: can_board
params.label: CAN transceiver
choices: the SN65HVD230 chip on a small adapter (the smallest capsule)
the common SN65HVD230 module (a bigger capsule)
params.help: The chip sits on the ESP32's back; the module beside it.

params.name: nav_top
params.label: Joystick: the stem's top above its base
params.help: Too short and its cap can't grip it (the model says so).
